narrative.title: Flagging Extreme Drift Between Sampled Sensors
narrative.scenario: A monitoring pipeline pairs each sample with every later sample and flags the pair when the earlier reading is more than twice the later one, which indicates a sensor drifting far out of scale. The audit needs the total number of such flagged pairs in the stream.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers, one sensor reading per sample.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of index pairs (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] > 2 * nums[j].
constraints: Doubling a reading may overflow a 32-bit integer

testCases.explanation: Both 3s at positions 1 and 3 exceed twice the trailing 1 at position 4, giving two flagged pairs.
The readings 4, 3 and 5 each outstrip twice the final tiny reading 1, so three pairs are flagged.

hintLevels: Level 1: As with counting out-of-order pairs, sorting the data while counting is the way to avoid a quadratic scan.
Level 2: Within each merge step, count the qualifying pairs by sweeping the sorted left half against a single forward-moving cursor over the sorted right half, then merge as usual.

Level 3: For each left value the qualifying count is how many right values are less than half of it - advance the cursor only in that direction, and widen the comparison before doubling so extreme or negative readings cannot overflow or invert.
